subject: Post-demo recap: procurement channel & hosting preference clarifications
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@novastore.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: procurement channel & hosting preference clarifications

Hi Sofia — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and three asks to help us accelerate procurement:

Summary from our call:
- NovaStore will run a 6–8 week pilot for product search reranking and embeddings-based similarity (approx. 500–1,000 queries/day).
- Procurement preference unclear between: Marketplace (AWS) vs direct PO to Redwood vs corporate card for POC spend.
- Hosting options we discussed: Hosted API (fast), Dedicated reserved pool (predictable throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem) for data-sensitive workflows.

What we need from you to finalize pricing packaging and procurement path:
1) Who is the procurement contact and preferred vendor onboarding portal (Coupa/Ariba/Procure)?
2) For pilot spend <$5k, is corporate card allowed, or do you require a PO even for POC?
3) Do you have any internal constraints that would force Private deployment (e.g., fixed-airgap, on-prem data residency)?

Attached: redwood_pricing_options_v3.pdf — short matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with commit vs on-demand pricing and typical transition paths.

Proposed next steps:
- If card is acceptable for the pilot, we recommend starting Hosted (on-demand) for fastest time-to-value, then transition to Dedicated (12-month commit) for production throughput.
- If PO/marketplace is required, we can prepare marketplace pricing and a commercial addendum — will need to know the preferred procurement flow so we can align invoice and SLA language.

Could you confirm the procurement contact and whether Marketplace is preferred? If you prefer, loop in your procurement lead and I’ll send a one-page vendor onboarding checklist to speed things up.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@novastore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-23T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement channel & hosting preference clarifications

Thanks Karthik — useful summary.

Answers inline:
1) Procurement contact for vendor onboarding is Miguel Ramos (cc'd below) — we run vendor onboarding through Coupa for most vendors but for cloud/marketplace purchases we sometimes use AWS Marketplace.
2) For pilots under $5k we can usually do card, but anything above that typically requires a PO + 30-day terms (finance policy).
3) We do have one product team that prefers data to stay in our VPC for PII-affiliated signals — would want to confirm whether Private deployment is needed, but for the initial pilot Hosted should be fine.

Attaching the vendor intake form they asked us to fill: novastore_vendor_form_filled.pdf

Can you send an estimated monthly run-rate for both an on-demand Hosted pilot and for a Dedicated 12-month reserved configuration (approx tokens/day and cost range)? That will help us choose the purchasing path.

Sofia Delgado
Senior Product Manager, NovaStore
sofia.delgado@novastore.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Miguel Ramos <miguel.ramos@novastore.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@novastore.com>
Date: 2027-08-23T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement channel & hosting preference clarifications

Hi Miguel — welcome, and thanks for jumping in. Quick alignment from our side based on your team's pilot / projected production profile:

Recommended path (pilot -> production):
- Pilot (0–8 weeks): Hosted API, on-demand billing. Low setup friction, immediate access to models + streaming responses. Estimated pilot run-rate: $1,200–$3,500/month depending on usage pattern (we modeled 500–1,000 queries/day with average 600 tokens per query).
- Production: Dedicated reserved pool (recommended for predictable latency and cost). Typical commitment tier for your projected throughput: 12-month committed capacity. Example ballpark: committed pool starting at $18,000/month (reduces token unit cost ~40% vs on-demand).
- Private deployment: only recommended if your security team requires VPC or on-prem isolation. Private has higher fixed engineering onboarding and infra fees — we can provide an SOC2 + KMS integration checklist if needed.

Procurement channel tradeoffs:
- AWS Marketplace: easier for customers already purchasing there; invoicing and billing go through AWS (different revenue recognition and pricing fences). Marketplace purchases often require Marketplace AMI/Listing setup and may take a few business days to enable.
- Direct PO: standard for enterprise deals, gives straightforward MSA + SOW and direct invoicing to finance.
- Card: fastest for low-dollar POCs (< $5k).

Action items I can take this week:
- Share a one-page vendor onboarding checklist and MSA draft for your legal team (I will include a DocuSign link).
- Populate HubSpot deal with recommended SKUs and sample invoice (link below).
- If you confirm Coupa as the vendor portal, we’ll provide the additional fields they request (W-9, EIN, primary contact, tax form).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345
Planned attachment: pilot_scope_and_mop.docx (short statement of work + Milestones of Performance).

If Miguel confirms the preferred path (Marketplace vs Direct PO) and shares the finance contact, we can produce a concise commercial summary for procurement this afternoon.

Best,
Karthik
From: Miguel Ramos <miguel.ramos@novastore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@novastore.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement channel & hosting preference clarifications

Thanks everyone — quick procurement notes and outstanding asks from finance: 

Procurement notes:
- Vendor onboarding: Coupa is our standard; vendor must submit W-9 and supplier bank details.
- PO routing: All POs will be issued to finance@novastore.com with a 30-day net by default.
- Marketplace vs direct: For pilots we prefer card, but for any ongoing subscription we require a PO. Finance is open to AWS Marketplace if Redwood can surface identical SKUs/pricing and provide AWS invoice mapping.

Outstanding items we need from Redwood:
1) W-9 / EIN and standard vendor banking info (ACH).
2) A short one-page summary of the pilot pricing (Hosted on-demand) and the committed Dedicated option with monthly totals and renewal/cancel terms.
3) A DocuSign link for your MSA + SOW so legal can start review.

If we get the items above, we can complete vendor onboarding via Coupa and issue a PO. For timeline: if we have the PO + signed MSA by Sep 10, we can start the pilot the week of Sep 13.

Miguel Ramos
Vendor Onboarding Lead, NovaStore
miguel.ramos@novastore.com
finance@novastore.com
